title: Add a monitor gate before certificate rotation
author: octocat
lead: The gate blocks the certificate repair it protects, and the new workflow call breaks replay for running workflows.

summary.whatItDoes: Adds a monitor check before `RotateCA` deploys new certificates. Operators can skip the check with a flag.
summary.why: The author says rotation must wait until all nodes trust the new root. Otherwise nodes lose API access.

gates.evidence: The gate runs before the deploy that clears its alert.
No replay test covers the changed child workflow call.
The PR body lists one staging rotation with a link to its run.
The PR body explains the node trust problem.
Each finding points to one call site.
History changes need a version gate.
Two incidents show rotations that started too early.
No log or metric shows when an operator skips the gate.
The Datadog monitor API is named, and the gate retries on errors.
The runbook now describes the skip flag.

walkthrough.problem: A root CA rotation can start before every node trusts the new root. Nodes then lose API access.
systemToday: An operator runs `ctl rotate-ca` for one cluster.
`RotateCA` then marks the new root as active.
walkthrough.coreIntuition: The gate is a wait loop in front of the deploy. It is safe only if the deploy cannot be what clears the alert.

solutionMap.solves: Waits until the trust monitor is OK.
Reads the monitor state for one cluster.
Lets an operator bypass a stuck gate.

walkthrough.flowchart:
flowchart LR
  CLI[ctl rotate-ca] --> L[ClusterLifecycle]
  L --> R[RotateCA]:::rc
  R --> G[Monitor gate]:::ask
  G --> D[Deploy ca_certs]

steps.title: Operator starts a rotation
steps.today: The CLI signals `ClusterLifecycle` with the target cluster.

steps.title: RotateCA calls the gate
steps.changed: It now waits on the monitor gate first, unless the skip flag is set.
steps.effect: A rotation can wait up to 48 hours before the deploy.

items.title: The gate blocks the certificate repair
items.whereThisFits: `RotateCA` runs after `ClusterLifecycle` selects a rotation. It now calls the gate before the `ca_certs` deploy.
items.whyItMatters: The monitor alerts when nodes trust different roots. The deploy is what fixes that state.
items.whyBad: While the monitor alerts, the gate retries for 48 hours. The deploy that would clear the alert never runs.
items.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant R as RotateCA
  participant G as Monitor gate
  participant D as ca_certs deploy
  R->>G: Check cluster
  G-->>R: Alert
  R->>G: Retry for 48h
  Note over R,D: Deploy never starts
items.fix: Deploy `ca_certs` first. Check the monitor before the new root becomes active.

comment.text: Can the gate run after the ca_certs deploy and before the new root becomes active? Right now the monitor can stay in Alert because the deploy that fixes it never runs. Monitor 123 shows 3 clusters in Alert: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/123

items.title: Running workflows fail after deploy
items.whereThisFits: The new gate call adds a child workflow command to `RotateCA` histories.
items.whyItMatters: Temporal replays each workflow against its recorded commands. A new command breaks running workflows.
items.whyBad: A running `RotateCA` replays on the new worker, meets an unexpected child workflow command, and its workflow task fails.

real.evidence: `atlas workflow list` shows no running `RotateCA` executions today.

items.fix: Wrap the call in `workflow.GetVersion` and add a replay test.

comment.text: This adds a child workflow command without workflow.GetVersion. A RotateCA that is running at deploy time will fail replay. Please add a version gate and a replay test.

items.title: Operators cannot see a skipped gate
items.whereThisFits: The skip flag bypasses the gate inside `RotateCA`.
items.whyItMatters: A skipped gate removes the only safety check. On-call needs to see that it happened.
items.whyBad: No log, metric, or event records the skip. I found no telemetry for it in the diff.

real.evidence: Query that settles it: search logs for `skip_gate` after a staging run.

items.fix: The author confirms where a skip is recorded.

comment.text: When an operator sets the skip flag, where can on-call see it? I did not find a log, metric, or event for the skip in this PR.

checked: PR diff, review threads, and CI checks at the head SHA.
Live `RotateCA` executions in staging and prod with `atlas workflow list`.
gaps: Skip telemetry: no staging run with the flag. Query: search logs for `skip_gate`.

skills.why: The PR changes a Temporal workflow.
skills.how: Checked version gates and replay coverage.
